title: Adani Energy Wins 25-Year Bengal Deal for 1,750 MW of Round-the-Clock Renewable Power
excerpt: The Letter of Award from WBSEDCL covers 1,750 MW from July 2028, with a 750 MW option that would take the total to 2,500 MW if exercised. No tariff or contract value was disclosed.
body:
• Adani Energy Solutions' subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions has won a Letter of Award to supply 1,750 MW of round-the-clock renewable power to West Bengal's state discom for 25 years.
  • A 750 MW greenshoe option, if the discom exercises it, would take the total to 2,500 MW — the option is not yet committed capacity.
  • Supply of the first 1,750 MW is scheduled to begin July 1, 2028; the optional 750 MW would start April 1, 2029.
  • The company did not disclose a tariff or contract value, so the revenue the deal will generate cannot be calculated from the announcement.

Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) said on Saturday, November 21, that its wholly owned subsidiary Powerpulse Trading Solutions Ltd (PTSL) has received a Letter of Award from West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Ltd (WBSEDCL) to supply 1,750 MW of renewable energy round-the-clock (RE-RTC) power for 25 years, according to the company's statement carried by IANS.

What was awarded — and what was not

The award covers 1,750 MW. The larger 2,500 MW figure in the company's headline combines that award with a 750 MW greenshoe option: additional capacity WBSEDCL may choose to take, not capacity already committed. PTSL emerged as the successful bidder through a competitive bidding process and an e-reverse auction, the company said. No tariff and no total contract value were disclosed, so the deal's revenue cannot be derived from the announcement — capacity in megawatts describes a rate of delivery, not a rupee figure.

When the power flows

Supply for the initial 1,750 MW is scheduled to commence on July 1, 2028. Supply for the additional 750 MW is scheduled from April 1, 2029, and only if the greenshoe option is exercised. Nothing in the award changes West Bengal's power supply before those dates. AESL said PTSL has tied up about 4.6 GW of solar and wind capacity and 3.5 GWh of battery energy storage capacity on the sourcing side — the combination that round-the-clock renewable supply requires, since solar and wind alone do not generate through the night.

"Round-the-clock renewable power will be critical to India's energy transition, combining the sustainability of renewables and optimising transmission systems usage."

— Kandarp Patel, CEO, Adani Energy Solutions

Where this sits in the business

AESL describes itself as the country's largest private transmission company, with a transmission network of 30,683 circuit kilometres and 146,585 MVA of transformation capacity, and a retail distribution business serving approximately 13 million consumers in metropolitan Mumbai and the Mundra SEZ, according to the ANI report of the announcement. The Bengal award adds to PTSL's book of long-term supply contracts with bulk consumers — industries, data centres, commercial establishments and distribution companies.

What to watch next

Two things will decide how large this deal becomes: whether WBSEDCL exercises the 750 MW greenshoe option, and whether the tariff and contract terms are disclosed in a later filing. Until then, the confirmed facts are the 1,750 MW award, the 25-year term, and a start date in mid-2028.
